memory_update.text: APEI is the cleanest US-listed direct customer signal for the LMS operating-layer node because Rasmussen is migrating from Blackboard to D2L Brightspace and adopting bundled AI tutoring, feedback, analytics, and content creation.

DCBO should remain in the LMS operating-layer universe as a US-listed AI-first LMS/product leader, but its primary exposure appears more enterprise-learning than university-specific and needs vertical verification.

NNI is a second-order campus infrastructure candidate: payments, tuition management, and education technology services may become integration points as LMS and student operating platforms consolidate workflows.

Several obvious LMS leaders are private or non-US primary-listed, including Instructure/Canvas, Anthology/Blackboard, and D2L; US-listed exposure may therefore appear through direct customers, adjacent SaaS platforms, payments, analytics, tutoring, and content tools rather than pure-play LMS vendors.

node: Learning-management systems expanding into institutional operating platforms
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the hypothesis that LMS platforms are becoming institutional operating layers through AI tutoring, feedback, analytics, content creation, payments, and workflow integrations. The strongest direct evidence is Rasmussen University, owned by American Public Education, selecting D2L Brightspace plus D2L Lumi, Creator+, Performance+, Lumi Tutor, and Lumi Feedback. Because several category leaders are private or non-US primary-listed, this pass emphasizes US-listed direct customers and adjacent platforms rather than only headline LMS vendors.
